book.name: The Tourney at Saltings Quay
book.text: At Saltings Quay, for St James, Sir Osbert Thorne reached the last four before Sir Antoine de Brisac put him out. He broke 6 lances and struck the helm once. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Antoine de Brisac. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Gilbert Stavely and Sir Raoul de Lisle prisoner. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Geoffrey Grayle.

book.name: The Tourney at Fennick
book.text: At Fennick, for Michaelmas, Sir Osbert Thorne rode in the first round and was put out by Sir John Esterling. He broke 3 lances. The prize went to Sir Louis Redvers. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Baudouin Fenwick and Sir Walter Thorne prisoner and beat Sir Humphrey Darnay from the saddle. His side carried the field. The heralds gave him the prize of the tourney.

book.name: The joust on the green at Fennick
book.text: At Fennick, for St Luke, Sir Osbert Thorne rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir Gilles Norreys. He broke 2 lances, struck the helm once and bore Sir Guillaume Haverill to the ground. He was himself borne down by Sir Gilles Norreys. The prize went to Sir Gilles Norreys. The heralds wrote well of his conduct.

book.name: The joust of the Drapers’ Company at Saltings Quay
book.text: At Saltings Quay, for Whitsun, Sir Osbert Thorne rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir Bertrand Hollin. He broke 5 lances and struck the helm 3 times. He was himself borne down by Sir Bertrand Hollin. He vowed to bear Sir Philippe de Brisac down, and did not. The prize went to Sir Bertrand Hollin.

book.name: The pas held by Sir Piers Challon
book.text: On the road to Sallowfield, Sir Osbert Thorne touched the shield of Sir Piers Challon at a bridge, and was turned back. He broke 1 lance and struck the helm once.

book.name: The Tourney at Sallowfield
book.text: At Sallowfield, for St James, Sir Osbert Thorne rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Gilbert Stavely. He broke no lance. The prize went to Sir Arnaud Kestrel. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Bertrand Aubrecy prisoner and beat Sir Bertrand Stavely from the saddle. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Arnaud Kestrel.

book.name: The joust of the Drapers’ Company at Port Lessing
book.text: At Port Lessing, for Lammas, Sir Osbert Thorne rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Guillaume Haverill. He broke 1 lance and struck the helm once. The prize went to Sir Guillaume Haverill.

book.name: The Tourney at Queenshythe
book.text: At Queenshythe, for St Luke, Sir Osbert Thorne rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Baudouin Fenwick. He broke 1 lance. He was himself borne down by Sir Baudouin Fenwick. The prize went to Sir Thibaut de Coucy-Lessard. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Bertrand Aubrecy and Sir John Kerville prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Jehan Thorne, and ransomed. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Jehan Thorne.

book.name: The Tourney at Sallowfield
book.text: At Sallowfield, for Eastertide, Sir Osbert Thorne reached the last four before Sir Thibaut de Coucy-Lessard put him out. He broke 1 lance and struck the helm once. He was himself borne down by Sir Thibaut de Coucy-Lessard. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Gilles Norreys. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Humphrey Orme prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Jehan Thorne, and ransomed. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Guillaume Haverill.

book.name: The joust on the green at Othery
book.text: At Othery, for Midsummer, Sir Osbert Thorne rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Piers Hollin. He broke no lance. He was himself borne down by Sir Piers Hollin. The prize went to Sir Piers Hollin.

book.name: The joust on the green at Othery
book.text: At Othery, for St James, Sir Osbert Thorne rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir John Esterling. He broke 2 lances and bore Sir John Kerville to the ground. He was himself borne down by Sir John Esterling. The prize went to Sir John Esterling.

book.name: The joust of the Drapers’ Company at Port Lessing
book.text: At Port Lessing, for Michaelmas, Sir Osbert Thorne rode in the first round and was put out by Sir William Fauconberg. He broke no lance. The prize went to Sir William Fauconberg.

book.name: The Tourney at Wystan’s Ford
book.text: At Wystan’s Ford, for Whitsun, Sir Osbert Thorne carried the prize. He broke 7 lances, struck the helm once and bore Sir Humphrey Darnay to the ground. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Thibaut Hollin and Sir Aymer Denholm prisoner and beat Sir Bertrand Stavely from the saddle. His side was beaten. The heralds gave him the prize of the tourney.

book.name: The joust on the green at Othery
book.text: At Othery, for Midsummer, Sir Osbert Thorne rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Edmund de Rochemont. He broke 1 lance and struck the helm once. The prize went to Sir Bertrand Stavely.

book.name: The Tourney at Fennick
book.text: At Fennick, for St James, Sir Osbert Thorne rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Antoine Fauconberg. He broke no lance. The prize went to Sir William Fauconberg. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Philippe Challon and Sir Alain de Saint-Aubin prisoner. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir William Fauconberg.

book.name: The Earl of Stane’s Tourney
book.text: At Castle Brede, for Lammas, Sir Osbert Thorne rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir Gilles Orme. He broke 3 lances and struck the helm once. He was himself borne down by Sir Gilles Orme. The prize went to Sir Gilles Orme. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Thibaut Hollin, Sir Piers Hollin and Sir Walter Hollin prisoner. His side carried the field. The heralds gave him the prize of the tourney. At the barriers he beat Sir Thibaut de Coucy-Lessard before Sir Jehan Quarles beat him.

book.name: The Tourney at Merrow
book.text: At Merrow, for Michaelmas, Sir Osbert Thorne reached the last four before Sir Bertrand Hollin put him out. He broke 3 lances and struck the helm 3 times. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Bertrand Hollin. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Roger de Montval, Sir Gilbert Stavely and Sir Antoine Fauconberg prisoner. The two sides were judged even. The heralds gave him the prize of the tourney.

book.name: The Tourney at Queenshythe
book.text: At Queenshythe, for Lady Day, Sir Osbert Thorne carried the prize. He broke 7 lances and struck the helm 4 times. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Bertrand Pemberton prisoner. The two sides were judged even. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Aymer Ingram.

book.name: The Tourney at Fennick
book.text: At Fennick, for Eastertide, Sir Osbert Thorne carried the prize. He broke 6 lances and bore Sir Piers Challon and Sir Thibaut Vane to the ground. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Alain de Saint-Aubin prisoner. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Bertrand Hollin.

book.name: The pas held by Sir Geoffrey Haverill
book.text: On the road to Ambry Cross, Sir Osbert Thorne touched the shield of Sir Geoffrey Haverill at a bridge, and was turned back. He broke 2 lances.

book.name: The Duke of Aumbry’s Tourney
book.text: At Ambry Cross, for Whitsun, Sir Osbert Thorne rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Walter Hollin. He broke 2 lances and struck the helm once. He was himself borne down by Sir Walter Hollin. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Jehan Quarles. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Walter Hollin prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Bertrand Hollin, and ransomed. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Bertrand Hollin. At the barriers he was beaten by Sir Thibaut Darnay. The prize of the axe went to Sir Walter Hollin.

book.name: The King’s Tourney at Midsummer
book.text: At Kingsmead, for Midsummer, Sir Osbert Thorne reached the last eight before Sir Thibaut Darnay put him out. He broke 3 lances and struck the helm once. He was himself borne down by Sir Thibaut Darnay. The prize went to Sir Bertrand Hollin. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Alain de Saint-Aubin prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Piers Hollin, and ransomed. The two sides were judged even. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Gilles Orme. At the barriers he beat Sir Enguerrand Ashcombe and Sir Guillaume Haverill, and was given the prize of the axe.

book.name: The Earl of Stane’s Tourney
book.text: At Castle Brede, for Lammas, Sir Osbert Thorne rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Aymer Denholm. He broke 1 lance and struck the helm once. He was himself borne down by Sir Aymer Denholm. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Jehan Quarles. In the tourney in the field he took nobody. He was taken himself, by Sir Walter Hollin, and ransomed. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Jehan Quarles. At the barriers he was beaten by Sir Jehan Quarles. The prize of the axe went to Sir Guillaume Haverill.

book.name: The pas held by Sir Geoffrey Sallow
book.text: On the road to Othery, Sir Osbert Thorne touched the shield of Sir Geoffrey Sallow at a bridge, and rode through. He broke 2 lances and struck the helm once.

book.name: The Tourney at Othery
book.text: At Othery, for Michaelmas, Sir Osbert Thorne carried the prize. He broke 6 lances and bore Sir Enguerrand Ashcombe to the ground. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Edmund de Rochemont prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Enguerrand Ashcombe, and ransomed. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Antoine de Brisac. It was thought a small field for a knight of his name.

book.name: A name
book.text: The heralds have begun to call him Sir Osbert Thorne the Generous.

book.name: The Tourney at Hollin Moor
book.text: At Hollin Moor, for Lady Day, Sir Osbert Thorne the Generous carried the prize. He broke 4 lances, struck the helm once and bore Sir Baudouin Fenwick to the ground. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Thibaut Hollin prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Jehan Thorne, and ransomed. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Louis Redvers. It was thought a small field for a knight of his name.

book.name: The Tourney at Sallowfield
book.text: At Sallowfield, for Eastertide, Sir Osbert Thorne the Generous carried the prize. He broke 6 lances. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Thibaut Hollin prisoner and beat Sir Reynold Fauconberg from the saddle. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Aymer Ingram. It was thought a small field for a knight of his name.

book.name: The Duke of Aumbry’s Tourney
book.text: At Ambry Cross, for Whitsun, Sir Osbert Thorne the Generous reached the last four before Sir Walter Hollin put him out. He broke 3 lances. He was himself borne down by Sir Walter Hollin. He vowed to bear Sir Walter Hollin down, and did not. The prize went to Sir Bertrand Hollin. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Walter Hollin prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Reynold Ingram, and ransomed. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Thibaut Darnay. At the barriers he beat Sir Jehan Quarles and Sir Gilles Orme, and was given the prize of the axe. The heralds wrote that his conduct was wanting.

book.name: The King’s Tourney at Midsummer
book.text: At Kingsmead, for Midsummer, Sir Osbert Thorne the Generous rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Guillaume Haverill. He broke no lance. The prize went to Sir Bertrand Hollin. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Baudouin Fenwick prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Everard Wyvenhoe, and ransomed. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Thibaut de Coucy-Lessard. At the barriers he beat Sir Baudouin Fenwick and Sir Raoul de Lisle, and was given the prize of the axe.

book.name: The pas held by Sir Humphrey Orme
book.text: On the road to Hollin Moor, Sir Osbert Thorne the Generous touched the shield of Sir Humphrey Orme at a bridge, and rode through. He broke 2 lances and bore Sir Humphrey Orme to the ground.

book.name: The Tourney at Hollin Moor
book.text: At Hollin Moor, for Lammas, Sir Osbert Thorne the Generous carried the prize. He broke 4 lances, struck the helm once and bore Sir Edmund de Rochemont and Sir Bertrand Aubrecy to the ground. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Bertrand Pemberton and Sir Geoffrey Haverill prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Fulk Lacy, and ransomed. The two sides were judged even. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Fulk Lacy. It was thought a small field for a knight of his name. The heralds wrote well of his conduct.

book.name: A dubbing
book.text: In the winter of his 6th year, Sir Osbert Thorne the Generous knighted his squire, Humphrey, who had served him 5 years.

book.name: The Duke of Aumbry’s Tourney
book.text: At Ambry Cross, for Whitsun, Sir Osbert Thorne the Generous rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir Gilles Orme. He broke 5 lances and struck the helm twice. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Gilles Orme. In the tourney in the field he took nobody. He was taken himself, by Sir Walter Hollin, and ransomed. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Humphrey Vane. At the barriers he was beaten by Sir Gilles Orme. The prize of the axe went to Sir Bertrand Hollin.

lastResult.prompt: Sir Bertrand Hollin’s lance took your horse in the chest. The heralds award you the bout, and the crowd waits to see how you take it.
lastResult.chose: Ask the heralds to strike his fault from the roll.
lastResult.text: The heralds agree. It is the talk of the feast.
